response.sql:
WITH team_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    team_id,
    AVG(w) as avg_wins,
    AVG(CASE WHEN g IS NOT NULL AND l IS NOT NULL AND l != 0 THEN (g - l) / CAST(l AS FLOAT) ELSE NULL END) as avg_ratio
  FROM manager_half
  WHERE team_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY team_id
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_wins) as mean_wins
  FROM team_stats
)
SELECT 
  ts.team_id,
  ts.avg_wins,
  ts.avg_ratio,
  ts.avg_wins - om.mean_wins as gap_from_mean
FROM team_stats ts
CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
WHERE ts.avg_wins > om.mean_wins
ORDER BY gap_from_mean DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Database supports NULLS LAST in ORDER BY; if not supported, substitute ORDER BY CASE WHEN gap_from_mean IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, gap_from_mean DESC
NULL values in w, g, and l represent missing data and should be excluded; the division (g − l) ÷ l is computed only when both g and l are non-NULL and l ≠ 0
'The mean of all teams' average wins' refers to the mean of each team's average wins (team-level aggregation), not the raw mean across all individual records

alternatives.interpretation: If 'the mean of all teams' average wins' means the overall mean of the w column across all manager_half records (ignoring team structure), replace the overall_mean CTE with: SELECT AVG(w) as mean_wins FROM manager_half. This interpretation seems less likely given the phrasing 'all teams' average wins'.
